solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In attempt to secure objective …

definitions.note: used as an adjective meaning fashionable

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the word for attempt wraps round the objective

parts.note: an attempt is a try
an objective is an end, an aim

explanation.surface: An unfinished sentence about trying to lock in a goal, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay; 'In' at the start is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is 'in' is currently fashionable, the same as being trendy.

clue.text: Closely follow what pops up in the tagliatelli

indicators.note: pops up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner peers at whatever surfaces in a dish of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'pops up' reads the letters ETAGLIAT from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive right behind another vehicle is to follow it too closely; the 'what' points to the wordplay.

clue.text: Previously promise to pay right state coffers

parts.note: ex means former, previously
a cheque is a written order promising payment

explanation.surface: A government once promised to pay back the right amount into public funds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exchequer is the UK government department managing public money.
explanation.definitionFit: The national treasury holding public funds is named the Exchequer in Britain.

clue.text: Politicians half quibbled after poster put up — such a disappointment

indicators.note: after says the politicians and the half follow the poster
in a down answer, put up means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a poster
MPs are Members of Parliament

indicators.note: half takes the first half of the word, four of its eight letters

explanation.surface: Politicians argue after a campaign poster goes up, and it all falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: DA (AD reversed by 'put up') comes first, then MPS and QUIB. A firework that fails to go off is the image behind the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An event that fails to live up to expectations is a letdown, like a wet firework that fizzles.

clue.text: … team sped off in a rush

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of team sped are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a team hurriedly sped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'sped off' (departed) but is the anagram signal for TEAMSPED.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden headlong charge of a crowd or herd is a mad rush.

clue.text: You once took in art, may be drama

indicators.note: took in means held inside, so the archaic you surrounds the rest

parts.note: thee is an archaic form of you

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of art could be another arrangement

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned address: you studied art, which might include drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You once' is archaic thee; 'may be' signals the rearrangement and 'took in' the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre as an art form is plays and performance, the same as drama.

clue.text: Nonsense being quiet on Boris Johnson's round wobbly bum

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent

indicators.note: round means the nickname goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: BoJo is the familiar nickname for the former UK prime minister Boris Johnson

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters of bum are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mocking jibe about silence and a former prime minister's wobbly backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbly' is the anagram signal; 'round' has the nickname for Boris Johnson, a former UK prime minister, wrap the result. 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless ritual or gibberish is nonsense, a common informal synonym.

clue.text: Sussex traditionally has more

indicators.note: has means the phrase contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A claim that the county of Sussex historically had a greater share of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'SussEX TRAditionally'. Sussex is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional or further is extra, so it can stand for more.

clue.text: Name for Goliath up astride horse

indicators.note: astride means sitting with legs either side, so the reversed word straddles the horse
in a down answer, up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Goliath is the setter of this puzzle, who refers to themself as me
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A giant gets up astride a horse, giving his name to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle is called Goliath, so the name stands for 'me'; 'up' reverses it to EM and 'astride' puts it either side.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a person whose name is given to something, or the word so derived.

clue.text: Possible price dip in South African novel

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the South African word

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent

indicators.note: possible means a potential arrangement of the letters of price dip

explanation.surface: A financial forecast of a price fall within South Africa's economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' is the anagram signal and 'in' puts the result inside the South African; 'novel' looks like an adjective but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a racy historical romance, a genre of novel with steamy seduction scenes.

clue.text: Put out where one might go

definitions.meaning: read as two words: inside a commode, the lidded chair holding a chamber pot, is where one might relieve oneself

explanation.surface: A bare instruction pairing being put out with a place to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into IN + COMMODE; a commode is a chair with a chamber pot built in.
explanation.definitionFit: To inconvenience someone is a formal synonym for putting them out; the second sense is a toilet joke.

clue.text: Catchword about bottom (but not top)

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards
the top of a down-reading word is its first letter, which is left off

explanation.surface: A query about a slogan concerning one's rear end, with a joking caveat.
explanation.walkthrough: '(but not top)' removes the B from BOTTOM, leaving OTTOM; 'about' then turns OTTOM round.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a short slogan or phrase adopted as a guiding principle, as a motto is.

clue.text: Happiness is having good shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A homely maxim that happiness comes from having a decent roof over your head.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight or joy, a synonym for happiness.

clue.text: Book and journal to cover armed conflict starting off

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so the journal word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a journal is a daily diary

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken off

parts.note: armed conflict is action, as in seeing action

explanation.surface: A writer's plan to produce a book and journal about a war that is just beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting off' drops the first letter of the armed-conflict word, and 'to cover' puts the journal around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is a particular kind of reference book.

clue.text: Puddings possess a certain fragrance …

parts.note: afters is British informal for dessert
to possess is to have

explanation.surface: Desserts with a particular scent, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented lotion used by men after shaving is a kind of fragrance.

clue.text: Starts on forbidden fruit, lacking in authentic luxury food

indicators.note: in means the picked letters go inside the word for authentic

parts.note: authentic means true, genuine

indicators.note: the starts of the three following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Eating forbidden fruit and missing out on real luxury food, an Eden-like temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts on' takes F, F and L from 'forbidden fruit, lacking'; these go between TRU and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffles are rare, costly fungi prized as a delicacy, the very definition of luxury eating.

clue.text: Provides the ultimate in coarse jokes

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its final one

parts.note: quips are witty jokes

explanation.surface: A comedian offers the very height of crude humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate in' looks like praise (the best of crude jokes) but simply takes the last letter of 'coarse'.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to supply or furnish them, so it means provides.

clue.text: … that of prior up to no good

indicators.note: a monk up to no good is in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: the smell of a monk up to mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' rearranges PRIORUPTO. The definition runs on from 14 down: 'a certain fragrance … that of' a dried flower mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of dried petals and spices gives off a sweet scent, so the fragrance meant is its one.

clue.text: For brunch, a steak's somewhat indecent

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that eating steak at brunch is slightly improper.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'brUNCH A STEak's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sexual restraint or modesty is immoral, so improper or indecent.

clue.text: Legal work is pants

definitions.meaning: a barrister's cases, the instructions handed over by a solicitor
underpants of a short close-fitting kind

explanation.surface: A grumble that working in law is rubbish, using British slang 'pants' for bad.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' means worthless or rubbish, which drives the surface, but here it means underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers take on cases called briefs; briefs are also short underpants.

clue.text: Dancing priests and fairies

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Clergy and fairies dancing together, a whimsical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are elves or small spirits, synonyms for fairies.

clue.text: Accentuate the negative part in bankruptcy

indicators.note: in places the word for part inside the word for bankruptcy

parts.note: financial ruin is bankruptcy
a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: Playing up the bad side of a role played in a business collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part in bankruptcy' reads as a role in a collapse, but 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep stressing an embarrassing fact to someone is to dwell on the negative, a common idiom.

clue.text: See 9
Put out vase: there's an improvement

indicators.note: out means wrong, so the letters of put are rearranged

parts.note: an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: Putting a vase out makes the room look better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like 'put out' (set out) but is the anagram signal on 'Put' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise or recovery in fortunes is a turn for the better, an improvement.

clue.text: Jobs by vault, said note

parts.note: jobs are posts, positions of employment

indicators.note: said means the following word is spoken, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a crypt is an underground vault

explanation.surface: Someone notes a few jobs going alongside a vault, like a mysterious memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies to CRYPT, whose sound gives the CRIPT ending of the written answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A PS is a note added at the end of a letter after the signature.

clue.text: See 3
My turn, keep quiet!

definitions.note: used as an exclamation of surprise

parts.note: it's your go means it's your turn
sh is the instruction to be silent

explanation.surface: A board-game player claims a turn and tells the others to hush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive, but it is the exclamation 'My!', meaning the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable as interjections.

clue.text: Clothes to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: Clothes that are something to show off about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it reverses BRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for dress or attire, especially distinctive clothing.

clue.text: Unwrapped fun DVD, but old man saying "ah" to see it

indicators.note: with the wrapping of each word taken off, only its middle letter is left

explanation.surface: Someone opens a fun DVD, while a doctor has an old man say 'ah'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwrapped' looks like opening a present but strips the outer letters of each of the five words, leaving U, V, U, L, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lobe hanging at the back of the throat shows when a patient opens wide and says 'ah'.

clue.text: Among stars, the boy's 13 (kind of)

indicators.note: among puts the next piece in the midst of the stars

parts.note: Taurus is the constellation of the Bull
read as 'the boy is', contracted to he's

explanation.surface: An astrological note that a boy is at home among the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' is the containment signal. The definition points to 13 across: a book of synonyms is a kind of dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A book listing words with similar meanings is a type of word reference, broadly a sort of lexicon.

clue.text: Status dictates that sensible logo be designed

indicators.note: designed means the letters are laid out to a new plan, rearranged

explanation.surface: A brand manager insists the company logo be designed sensibly, as befits its status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges SENSIBLELOGOBE; 'be' belongs to the letters, not the surface grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase says privilege brings responsibility: high rank requires honourable conduct.
